transcript:
[00:00] Alex Mercer: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Alex from Redwood, AE on the account. Priya our SE is here to do the deep demo. Quick intro round...
[00:12] Jared Liao: Jared here, CTO at NimbleRetail. We're looking at automating order enrichment and insurance claims for returns, and worried about hallucinations and strict schema outputs.
[00:23] Maya Chen: Hi, Maya - Head of ML. We have a current POC with OpenAI for extraction but we keep getting malformed JSON and the post-processing is painful.
[00:36] Alex Mercer: Totally. Today we'll show structured output mode, function-calling examples, and how Console + Optimize can reduce cost and keep outputs strict. Priya, want to take it?
[00:44] Priya Raman: Sure. Jumping in - I'll share my screen - demo deck link: https://redwood.demo/structured-output (note: demo link placeholder) - first, JSON mode - you can define a schema to constrain outputs, enforce types, and Redwood runtime will validate and optionally fail-safe to a handler.
[01:05] Priya Raman: Example: we define a schema for "order_enrichment" with fields: order_id (string), items (array of objects), fraud_score (number), recommended_action (enum). When the model returns, we run schema validation server-side and will either accept, coerce, or call a fallback tool.
[01:30] Sam Ortiz: Is that a runtime schema or baked into the prompt?
[01:34] Priya Raman: It's part of the API call - JSON mode has a schema parameter plus validation policy. You can set strict enforcement -> reject outputs that don't match, or best-effort -> attempt to coerce. That reduces your post-processing.
[01:50] Jared Liao: What happens when the model hallucinates a field like an extra item id? Do you drop it or reject?
[01:56] Priya Raman: Depends on your policy. In strict mode it'll reject and trigger an error path; in best-effort it'll try to coerce types and remove unknown keys. You can also wire an automatic function call to reconcile with your product DB to verify item ids.
[02:15] Alex Mercer: This is where function-calling comes in. We showed a sample earlier - Redwood can call internal tools/functions (your microservices) with strongly-typed payloads. If the model asks to call "get_item_details", it invokes the function with validated args.
[02:34] Maya Chen: Are those function calls executed in Redwood's control plane or do they proxy to our VPC?
[02:38] Priya Raman: Good question. For private customers you can have function endpoints in your VPC and Redwood will call via a customer-configured private egress or connector. For hosted customers we can proxy or advise using signed webhook endpoints. We also support HMAC signing on calls.
[02:56] Jared Liao: What about latency? If we keep calling internal APIs per token that could kill our p99.
[03:02] Priya Raman: Yep. Typical pattern: do minimal verification calls. Use local validation + caching for item meta to avoid excessive round trips. Redwood Optimize suggests batching strategies and cache TTLs based on traffic to balance p99 and unit cost.
[03:20] Alex Mercer: Also dedicated capacity helps because you can guarantee lower tail latency. If you want predictable throughput for this enrichment pipeline, Dedicated is often the way.
[03:30] Sam Ortiz: Cost delta vs hosted?
[03:33] Alex Mercer: Hosted is simple - pay per token - but for constant heavy throughput Dedicated with reserved GPUs plus Optimize config usually lowers unit cost significantly. We'll send a cost model.
[03:42] Maya Chen: Can you demo the actual JSON mode sample?
[03:45] Priya Raman: Yep. Switching to the notebook... (screen share) here's an API call: 
POST /v1/generate 
body: {"model":"redwood-structured-1","json_schema":{...},"mode":"json"} 
We run and the model returns nearly valid JSON but with a date field as string instead of ISO - Redwood's coercion fixed it to ISO and set an audit flag.
[04:20] Maya Chen: Nice. Do you log the coerced fields and the reasoning?
[04:24] Priya Raman: Console shows token-level diffs, validation errors, and a trace linking the request to the function call. You can also instrument a webhook for validation failures.
[04:38] Jared Liao: About hallucinations - are there guardrails beyond schema? For example, ensuring PII not returned, or model won't invent transaction IDs.
[04:46] Priya Raman: Yes - we have policy hooks and redactors. At runtime you can configure allow-lists/block-lists for fields, entity detection, and set a "never return" policy for PII. Also, you can enforce that certain IDs must be verified via a function call before accepting.
[05:05] Alex Mercer: We also do output sampling and quality monitoring - Redwood Optimize will flag regressions on your eval set and can trigger rollbacks.
[05:12] Sam Ortiz: Can you show function-calling in action 	6.g., model calls a function to fetch order history then returns enriched JSON?
[05:18] Priya Raman: Yes - demo time. (runs demo) Model invoked function get_order_history({order_id: "12345"}) -> Redwood called your endpoint (demo uses mocked endpoint). The function returned 3 items. Model then produced a validated JSON payload with recommended_action: "flag_for_review" because fraud_score > 0.8.
[05:52] Speaker 1: [inaudible] mock response was, uh, slightly different - transcription note.
[06:00] Maya Chen: In your example where the function returns conflicting data, which source wins? Model or function?
[06:06] Priya Raman: Functions are authoritative for returned structured data - if a function returns authoritative product details we can prefer function outputs. But you can define merge policies: prefer function, prefer model, or custom resolver.
[06:20] Jared Liao: Can Redwood enforce schema changes over time? We have evolving order schemas and need to version them.
[06:27] Priya Raman: Yes - Console supports versioned schemas and rollouts. You can pin a schema to a route and can do canary deployments of new schema versions with traffic percentage. If validation error rate spikes, auto rollback.
[06:43] Alex Mercer: Another feature - you can store example-based guards: add golden prompts / test cases in Console and Redwood Optimize will run them routinely to catch regressions.
[06:52] Sam Ortiz: Security questions: SOC2, KMS, and audit logs - what do you provide?
[06:58] Priya Raman: We provide SOC2 Type II, ISO attestations for enterprise customers, KMS integration for key wrapping, and immutable audit trails for every function call and output. For Private deployments we can integrate with your on-prem HSM. We'll share the security pack.
[07:18] Jared Liao: Data residency 	64 we need EU data kept in EU. Is that supported?
[07:23] Alex Mercer: Yes - region routing policies let you route requests to EU-hosted clusters and you can pin model variants by region. Private deployment gives you full control over residency.
[07:35] Maya Chen: Back to runtime - how do you prevent token leakage in logs or traces?
[07:40] Priya Raman: Redaction policies at ingestion, token-level masking in traces, and role-based access in Console. Logs can be configured to scrub PII before long-term retention.
[07:54] Jared Liao: We need to validate on our own data - can we run benchmarks?
[07:58] Priya Raman: Absolutely - typical pilot: we set up a small dedicated pool, you send a sample traffic replay, and we run p50/p95/p99 and unit cost analysis plus accuracy on your eval set.
[08:12] Alex Mercer: We'll propose a 2-week pilot with a small dedicated instance. Pricing and SOW in follow-up.
[08:18] Maya Chen: One more on function-calling security - do you support mTLS to our endpoints?
[08:23] Priya Raman: Yes, mTLS and IP allowlists for VPC connectors. For webhook-style calls we support HMAC verification and request signing.
[08:34] Sam Ortiz: Any limits on number of functions or concurrency?
[08:38] Priya Raman: No hard-coded limits 	6 concurrency tied to your capacity tier. Dedicated gives you predictable concurrency and you can set rate limits on per-route basis.
[08:50] Alex Mercer: Quick demo of guardrail policies - setting strict JSON schema + fallback to queued review.
[08:56] Priya Raman: (shows Console) Here's a policy: if validation fails -> send to review queue + notify slack + call fallback function to create a ticket. You can configure sampling to inspect some accepted outputs for quality.
[09:15] Maya Chen: The Console UI looks useful. Is there an API to automate rollouts?
[09:19] Priya Raman: Yep - everything is API-first: rollouts, schema updates, policy changes are exposed. We recommend using CI to push schema changes and run staged rollouts.
[09:28] Jared Liao: For our engineering team, how much work to integrate? We have node microservices and a k8s cluster.
[09:35] Priya Raman: Integration surface is small: SDK + a few webhooks/functions. We'll provide a sample node client and a helm chart for the connector. The heavy lifting is schema design and deciding which calls are function-proxied vs validated locally.
[09:50] Alex Mercer: Time for questions from the team?
[09:54] Sam Ortiz: Do you have an example of the schema file?
[09:57] Priya Raman: Yes - here's a snippet (reads): {"type":"object","properties":{"order_id":{"type":"string"},"items":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"object","properties":{"sku":{"type":"string"},"qty":{"type":"integer"}}}},"fraud_score":{"type":"number"},"recommended_action":{"type":"string","enum":["approve","flag_for_review","cancel"]}}}
[10:28] Maya Chen: If the model tries to invent a SKU, can you map to nearest existing SKU?
[10:33] Priya Raman: You could call a function that uses fuzzy matching against your product catalog and return a confidence score. Redwood can then include that resolution in the final payload and set a confidence field.
[10:44] Jared Liao: Any built-in eval tooling?
[10:47] Priya Raman: Yes - Redwood Optimize includes eval harnesses, test suites, and regression alerts tied to golden test sets. We also surface token-level cost per test.
[11:03] Alex Mercer: We should talk timeline - what are you looking at for a pilot?
[11:07] Jared Liao: We'd like to start by end of month, but need security review first.
[11:12] Alex Mercer: Sounds good. We'll send SOC2 + data flow docs and propose pilot dates.
[11:18] Priya Raman: Demo wrap-up - quick run showing failure handling: model returned malformed date/time and Console flagged it, auto-coerced with audit flag and sent a message to the review queue. (shows timeline)
[11:40] Sam Ortiz: The audit trail - can we export it to our SIEM?
[11:44] Priya Raman: Yes - logs and traces can be pushed to your SIEM or a cloud storage bucket.
[11:50] Maya Chen: My last question - do you support structured output from multimodal inputs (like images of receipts)?
[11:56] Priya Raman: Roadmap includes it; current beta supports image inputs with structured extraction for select partners. We can include you in the beta if needed.
[12:08] Jared Liao: Great. On governance - can we restrict which Redwood staff can see logs for our account?
[12:12] Alex Mercer: Yes - RBAC and support access controls; for Private deployments support access can be limited and audited.
[12:20] Maya Chen: Anything else on Optimize?
[12:23] Priya Raman: Optimize recommends quantization profiles and batching configs per workload and shows expected latency/cost tradeoffs. It can also recommend fallback model variants for lower cost SLOs.
[12:40] Sam Ortiz: Will the function calling work with our internal auth flows? We use OAuth2 and session-based tokens.
[12:46] Priya Raman: We support passing your tokens in headers; for longer flows we recommend a service-to-service account with short-lived tokens. We'll show patterns in the integration doc.
[12:58] Speaker 2: [background] fence, sorry - small noise.
[13:02] Alex Mercer: Ok let's do a quick recap and next steps.
[13:06] Alex Mercer: Recap: 1) Redwood JSON mode + schema validation can reduce post-processing and hallucination. 2) Function calling enables authoritative lookups and richer payloads. 3) Console provides traces, rollouts, and policy enforcement. 4) Optimize recommends costs/batching and helps plan Dedicated.
[13:28] Priya Raman: Next steps: we'll share pricing + security docs and schedule a pilot benchmark. Links: demo notebook (https://redwood.demo/notebooks/json-function-demo), benchmark sheet (https://drive.fake/benchmark-nimble).
[13:44] Jared Liao: Thanks - we need SOC2 docs and a sample SOW.
[13:48] Alex Mercer: We'll send those. Any final questions?
[13:52] Maya Chen: No more from me.
[13:55] Sam Ortiz: Looks good.
[13:57] Alex Mercer: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up over email. End call.
